name: Istio
tagline: Routes, secures and observes service-to-service traffic with Envoy.

howItWorks.title: What it is and where it sits
howItWorks.body:
Istio adds a programmable proxy layer beside every workload, so apps need no code changes.
It works at L4 for mTLS and TCP policy, and L7 for HTTP and gRPC routing.
The control plane is istiod; the data plane is Envoy sidecars or ambient ztunnel and waypoint proxies.
It lives in the Platform layer and complements Kubernetes Services rather than replacing them.
Use it when you need canaries, mutual TLS and uniform telemetry across many services.

howItWorks.title: Components and architecture
howItWorks.body:
istiod is one binary: xDS config server, certificate authority and sidecar injection webhook.
Envoy sidecars intercept pod traffic with iptables redirect and enforce routes and policy.
Ingress and egress gateways are standalone Envoys at the mesh edge.
Ambient mode splits the mesh: a node-level ztunnel for L4 and optional waypoint proxies for L7.
Sidecars cost memory in every pod; ambient avoids that cost but is a different operating model.

howItWorks.title: Request flow
howItWorks.body:
The app calls a Service name as usual; the sidecar intercepts the outbound connection.
Envoy matches host and path against VirtualService rules and picks a destination subset.
DestinationRule settings apply: load balancing, connection pool, outlier detection.
Envoy opens mTLS to the endpoint using its SPIFFE identity certificate.
The server-side proxy checks AuthorizationPolicy, then hands the request to the app.

howItWorks.title: Configuration model
howItWorks.body:
Gateway opens ports and hosts at the edge; VirtualService binds routes to it or to mesh traffic.
DestinationRule defines subsets by pod label plus traffic policy; apply it before weighted routes.
ServiceEntry adds external hosts; Sidecar resource limits what each proxy loads.
PeerAuthentication sets mTLS mode; AuthorizationPolicy allows by identity, method and path.
Gateway API resources are the newer, vendor-neutral way to express edge and mesh routing.

howItWorks.title: Connecting to its neighbours
howItWorks.body:
In front (Edge): an external balancer or NGINX forwards to the ingress gateway Service.
Every Gateway is backed by a Service of type LoadBalancer; without a balancer, use NodePort or MetalLB.
Behind (Platform): sidecars route to Kubernetes Services and pods using the VirtualService rules.
Outside the mesh, ServiceEntry adds external hosts; Prometheus and Grafana (Operators) consume mesh metrics.
An east-west gateway on port 15443 links clusters on different networks.
Sidecar mode suits fine-grained L7 per pod; ambient suits low overhead and mostly L4 mTLS.

howItWorks.title: Security
howItWorks.body:
istiod issues short-lived workload certificates; rotation is automatic.
PERMISSIVE accepts plaintext and mTLS; STRICT demands mTLS. Migrate in that order.
AuthorizationPolicy is default-allow until an ALLOW policy selects a workload; then deny the rest.
RequestAuthentication validates JWTs; pair it with AuthorizationPolicy to require them.
Multi-cluster trust needs a shared root CA so certificates verify across clusters.

howItWorks.title: Resilience, HA and scaling
howItWorks.body:
Run two or more istiod replicas with a PodDisruptionBudget; proxies keep last config if it is down.
Timeouts, retries and outlier detection live in VirtualService and DestinationRule.
Set retry attempts explicitly; stacked retries across hops multiply load.
Scale ingress gateways with HPA like any Deployment.
Upgrade with revisions: install the new control plane, move namespaces by label, roll pods.

howItWorks.title: Observability
howItWorks.body:
Every sidecar emits request count, duration and size metrics for Prometheus.
Access logs and Envoy tracing headers feed Grafana, Jaeger or Tempo and Kiali.
Golden signals come free per workload without touching application code.
Alert on 5xx rate and request p95 per destination service.

howItWorks.title: Failure modes and troubleshooting
howItWorks.body:
istioctl analyze finds config errors before they cause failures.
istioctl proxy-status shows which proxies are STALE or not SYNCED with istiod.
503 with NR means no route; UH means no healthy upstream; UF is upstream connection failure.
A missing DestinationRule subset is the classic cause of 503s after a VirtualService change.
Strict mTLS resets plaintext callers; check that clients are injected before enforcing.

howItWorks.title: Alternatives
howItWorks.body:
Linkerd: choose it for a smaller, simpler mesh with automatic mTLS.
Cilium service mesh: choose it for an eBPF data plane without sidecars.
Consul: choose it when VMs and Kubernetes share one mesh.
No mesh: Kubernetes Services plus Ingress are enough when you do not need mTLS or traffic splitting.

flow: The client calls the Service name as normal.
The sidecar intercepts the outbound connection through iptables redirect.
Envoy matches the host and applies VirtualService route rules.
Weights pick the subset: stable or canary.
DestinationRule applies load balancing, pool limits and outlier detection.
Envoy opens mTLS to the endpoint with its SPIFFE certificate.
The server sidecar checks AuthorizationPolicy and forwards to the app.
From outside, traffic enters through the ingress gateway first.

deploy.summary: Install Istio on one cluster, split traffic, expose the gateway, enforce mTLS.
prerequisites: Linux nodes with sudo and SSH
Placeholders in <angle brackets> are yours to set

steps.title: Harden SSH on every node
steps.code:
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C ops@<HOST> -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
ssh-copy-id -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub <USER>@<NODE_IP>
printf 'PasswordAuthentication no\nPermitRootLogin no\n' | sudo tee /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/10-harden.conf
sudo sshd -t && sudo systemctl reload ssh
steps.note: Test key login in a second session before reloading. The unit is sshd on RHEL-family hosts.

steps.title: Static address and firewall
steps.code:
# /etc/netplan/50-static.yaml (placeholders)
# network: {version: 2, ethernets: {ens18: {addresses: [<NODE_IP>/24], routes: [{to: default, via: <GW>}], nameservers: {addresses: [<DNS_IP>]}}}}
sudo netplan apply
sudo ufw allow from <LB_CIDR> to any port 30000:32767 proto tcp
sudo ufw allow from <NODE_CIDR> to any port 6443,10250 proto tcp
steps.note: Add a DNS A record for the API server. Restrict the NodePort range to your load balancer.

steps.title: Install istioctl and the control plane
steps.code:
curl -L https://istio.io/downloadIstio | ISTIO_VERSION=1.24.1 sh -
cd istio-1.24.1 && export PATH=$PWD/bin:$PATH
istioctl x precheck
istioctl install --set profile=default -y
kubectl -n istio-system get pods
steps.note: On bare metal there is no cloud LoadBalancer, so expose the ingress gateway through a NodePort or MetalLB.

steps.title: Inject the sidecar by annotation
steps.code:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: frontend-v1, namespace: shop}
spec:
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: frontend, version: v1}}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: {app: frontend, version: v1}
      annotations:
        sidecar.istio.io/inject: "true"
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: frontend
          image: <REGISTRY>/frontend:1.0.0
steps.note: First run kubectl label namespace shop istio-injection=enabled. Pods must show 2/2 ready.

steps.title: DestinationRule: subsets and outlier detection
steps.note: Apply this before the VirtualService. A missing subset returns 503 with NR or UH flags.

steps.title: VirtualService: 90/10 to 0/100
steps.note: Raise canary to 50, then 100, by editing weights. Blue-green is 100/0 flipped to 0/100 in one apply.

steps.title: STRICT mTLS and AuthorizationPolicy
steps.code:
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1
kind: PeerAuthentication
metadata: {name: default, namespace: shop}
spec: {mtls: {mode: STRICT}}
---
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata: {name: frontend-allow, namespace: shop}
spec:
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: frontend}}
  action: ALLOW
  rules:
    - from: [{source: {principals: ["cluster.local/ns/istio-system/sa/istio-ingressgateway-service-account"]}}]
      to: [{operation: {methods: ["GET"]}}]
steps.note: Once any ALLOW policy matches a workload, everything else is denied. Confirm meshed clients first.

steps.title: Expose the ingress gateway
steps.code:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1
kind: Gateway
metadata: {name: shop-gw, namespace: shop}
spec:
  selector: {istio: ingressgateway}
  servers:
    - port: {number: 80, name: http, protocol: HTTP}
      hosts: ["shop.example.com"]
---
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1
kind: VirtualService
metadata: {name: frontend-edge, namespace: shop}
spec:
  hosts: ["shop.example.com"]
  gateways: [shop-gw]
  http:
    - route: [{destination: {host: frontend, subset: stable}}]
EOF
kubectl -n istio-system patch svc istio-ingressgateway -p '{"spec":{"type":"NodePort"}}'
NP=$(kubectl -n istio-system get svc istio-ingressgateway -o jsonpath='{.spec.ports[?(@.name=="http2")].nodePort}')
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -H 'Host: shop.example.com' http://<NODE_IP>:$NP/
steps.note: Point an external proxy at <NODE_IP>:$NP; on cloud keep LoadBalancer. shop.example.com is a placeholder.

verify: istioctl proxy-status shows every proxy SYNCED.
istioctl x describe pod <frontend-pod> -n shop shows STRICT mTLS and weights.
curl -H 'Host: shop.example.com' http://<NODE_IP>:$NP/ returns 200 via the gateway.
kubectl -n shop get pods shows 2/2 ready for injected workloads.
pitfalls: A missing subset in the DestinationRule returns 503 with NR or UH response flags.
Enabling STRICT before every client is meshed resets plaintext callers.
Annotation needs the namespace injection label or revision; restart existing pods.
The Gateway selector must match the gateway pod labels, or no listener appears.
Clusters with different root CAs cannot establish cross-cluster mTLS.
A Gateway host that does not match the VirtualService hosts returns 404.
Default retries plus your own retries multiply load; set attempts explicitly.
keyPoints: VirtualService and DestinationRule drive canary, blue-green and weighted splits.
The ingress gateway is a Service exposed by LoadBalancer or NodePort.
Strict mTLS plus AuthorizationPolicy decide which identity may call what.
Sidecar or ambient: same control plane, different data-plane cost.
quickDeploy: Install istioctl and the control plane.
Label the namespace for sidecar injection.
Apply DestinationRule subsets, then weighted VirtualService.
Expose the gateway, then enforce STRICT mTLS.
osiNote: mTLS and TCP policy at L4; HTTP and gRPC routing at L7.
production: Run two or more istiod replicas with a PodDisruptionBudget.
Pin the Istio version; upgrade with revisions and canary the data plane.
Set explicit timeouts, retries and outlier detection on every hot route.
Keep PERMISSIVE until every client is meshed, then enforce STRICT.
Alert on 5xx rate, request p95 and proxies not SYNCED in istioctl proxy-status.
